meta.blog-sprila-2027.html.title: SPRILA 2027: a new round of charging infrastructure funding for hotels · Lemnion
meta.blog-sprila-2027.html.description: The SPRILA scheme is expected to reopen at the end of January 2027. The 2026 budget is oversubscribed. What the new round means for charging points and batteries at your hotel.
blog-sprila.intro: The budget for charging infrastructure in the current SPRILA round has been oversubscribed since 20 November 2026. Anyone who still wanted a grant this autumn for charging points in the car park now joins a waiting list. The new round is expected to open at the end of January 2027. For hotels preparing their car park for electric guests and staff, that is the moment to get the application ready. Below you can read exactly what has changed, what is coming in 2027 and what to watch out for.
blog-sprila.kort-li1: The budget for charging stations and batteries in the 2026 round is oversubscribed. Applications are still possible, but are processed in order of receipt.
blog-sprila.kort-li2: The SPRILA is expected to reopen at the end of January 2027. Budget has been reserved through 2030.
blog-sprila.kort-li3: In 2027, small applications up to € 25,000 can be submitted within 13 weeks of completing the installation.
blog-sprila.kort-li4: Applications above € 25,000 must be submitted before you place the order. A signed quote counts as an order.
blog-sprila.kort-li5: From 1 January 2027, the EPBD IV requirements for existing hotels with more than 20 parking spaces become stricter. The subsidy scheme and the obligation therefore coincide.
blog-sprila.wat-p1: The Subsidy Scheme for Private Charging Infrastructure at Businesses (SPRILA) covers part of the cost of charging points on your own or leased land. The scheme is intended for businesses with their own electric vehicles, for employers with staff who drive electric and for businesses with customers who drive electric. That is exactly why it fits the hotel industry so well: you charge for your guests, your staff and the taxis waiting at the door.
blog-sprila.wat-p2: Private charging infrastructure means the points are not accessible to everyone at all times. Your guests may charge during their stay, but the charging points may not be public 24 hours a day. Once the grant has been awarded, your charging stations may also not be listed as publicly accessible for 24 months. At most they may be listed as limited access.
blog-sprila.wat-p3: SMEs receive double the amount per charging station compared with large companies. You need to include an SME declaration. Note the state aid ceiling: a maximum of 40% of eligible costs for SMEs and 20% for large companies. RVO will reduce the grant if you exceed it.
blog-sprila.stand-p1: The 2026 round opened on 20 January and closes on 18 December at 12:00. The total budget is €122,500,000. On 20 November 2026 the budget for charging stations for businesses outside public transport became oversubscribed by €2,263,602. The battery budget is also oversubscribed, by €817,810.
blog-sprila.stand-p2: What does that mean in practice?
blog-sprila.stand-li1: You can still apply. RVO assesses applications by date of receipt, and budget can be freed up when applications are rejected or not processed.
blog-sprila.stand-li2: Applications under €25,000 can be submitted until 18 December 2026, 12:00. They will be assessed in the new round from the end of January 2027 under the carry-over rule. If your installation was completed before 1 November 2026, submit this year.
blog-sprila.stand-li3: For applications above €25,000 the charging station budget is oversubscribed. Budget remains only for DC charging stations for public transport concession holders and coach companies.
blog-sprila.verand-h1: The scheme is expected to open at the end of January.
blog-sprila.verand-p1: RVO has not announced an exact date yet. Keep an eye on the RVO page and do not wait until the opening to prepare, because the 2026 budget was already oversubscribed in November.
blog-sprila.verand-p2: The funds are reserved under the multi-year programme for recycling truck toll revenue (Terugsluis vrachtwagenheffing) and the Climate and Energy Fund. That creates room for a multi-year plan across several locations instead of squeezing everything into one round.
blog-sprila.verand-h3: The submission window for small applications becomes 13 weeks after installation.
blog-sprila.verand-p3: Applying for less than €25,000 in 2027? You may install first and submit afterwards, within 13 weeks of the date the work was completed. That is practical for hotels that have already installed ahead of the EPBD IV deadline of 1 January 2027.
blog-sprila.verand-h4: The 2027 amounts are not yet known.
blog-sprila.verand-p4: The list of grant amounts on the RVO website covers 2026. Do not count blindly on €800 per AC charging point or €85 per kWh of battery capacity. RVO publishes the amounts per year and can adjust categories, as it did in 2026 with the DC categories and the battery conditions.
blog-sprila.verand-h5: Above €25,000: apply first, then place the order.
blog-sprila.verand-p5: Under the European state aid rules you may only invest after submitting the application. RVO regards a signed quote as an order placed. So deliberately leave your quote unsigned until the application has been submitted.
blog-sprila.epbd-h2: Why this coincides with a deadline for hotels
blog-sprila.epbd-p1: From 1 January 2027, stricter requirements apply to existing non-residential buildings with more than 20 parking spaces: at least one charging point per ten parking spaces, or cable ducts for half of the parking spaces. For a hotel with 60 parking spaces that means six charging points, or a preparation showing that they can be installed later.
blog-sprila.epbd-p2: The two developments reinforce each other. You have to do something about your car park anyway, and the scheme that makes it affordable opens at the same moment. Anyone who starts orienting in January loses valuable weeks. Preparing the application takes two and a half to three hours according to RVO, but collecting the quote, datasheets, the grid operator contract and the capacity calculation usually takes longer.
blog-sprila.reken-h2: Worked example for an SME hotel
blog-sprila.reken-p1: Suppose you want twelve charging points for guests, installed as six dual posts of 2 x 11 kW. At the 2026 amounts that gives €1,600 per post, €9,600 in total.
blog-sprila.tabel-bron: Source: SPRILA, RVO.nl (2026 amounts, checked 23 November 2026). The 2027 amounts have not been published yet.
blog-sprila.reken-p2: If you also want a battery to absorb peaks and charge during off-peak hours, a separate threshold applies. The battery grant is at least €25,000 in combination with newly installed charging infrastructure. At €85 per kWh for SMEs that means a battery of at least 295 kWh. A 100 kWh battery does not reach that threshold; a 300 kWh battery yields €25,500. Together that comes to €35,100 in grants.
blog-sprila.reken-p3: Two caveats apply to that amount. A maximum of 1,000 kWh of battery capacity is eligible, so up to €85,000 for SMEs. And at least 70% of the discharged energy must demonstrably go to the subsidised charging stations. A battery that mainly supplies the building therefore does not fit this scheme.
blog-sprila.valk-p1: For applications above €25,000 this removes your entitlement to the grant.
blog-sprila.valk-p2: The grant per location must be at least €2,500. For SMEs that means at least four 11 kW AC charging stations (€3,200). With three you reach €2,400 and fall outside the scheme.
blog-sprila.valk-p3: Your charging stations may not be registered as publicly accessible for 24 months. Charging for guests is fine; a point that anyone can use at any time is not.
blog-sprila.valk-p4: Will your connection need to be upgraded because of the charging points or the battery? Check in advance whether your region has an overloaded grid. If the charging infrastructure requires more than 50% of your contracted transport capacity, you must include a capacity calculation showing it will work within 24 months.
blog-sprila.valk-p5: The charging infrastructure must always be connected to the internet and communicate via OCPP 1.6 or higher. For a battery you must also register it on Energieleveren, and the C value may be no more than 0.5, except for an integrated battery.
blog-sprila.advies-h2: What I advise hotels to do now
blog-sprila.advies-p1: Do not start thinking in January; start preparing in December. Have a design made and a quote drawn up that you do not sign yet. Decide in advance whether you want charging points only or a battery as well, because that choice determines whether you reach the €25,000 threshold and whether you end up in the small or the large application.
blog-sprila.advies-p2: Already completed the installation and staying below €25,000? Submit by 18 December 2026 at the latest, so your application is included in the first assessment of the new round. Above €25,000, focus on the opening at the end of January and make sure your application is complete on day one.
blog-sprila.advies-p3: And treat the 2027 amounts as an unknown. A business case that only works with the 2026 amounts is not a business case. Calculate the investment you will make anyway, and regard the grant as an accelerator.
blog-sprila.meer-p: The official conditions and the current budget status are on the SPRILA page of RVO. The EPBD IV requirements are in the guidance on charging infrastructure at buildings.
